files.role: Public wrappers and trait conversions between flat protobuf fields/dictionary metadata and Lance core field trees; arena reconstruction preserves historical duplicate-ID tie-breaking. No file IO is performed.
ranges: SPDX and imports connect Arrow extension-name metadata, core Dictionary/Encoding/Field/LogicalType/Schema, Error/Result, HashMap and generated file protobuf. These conversions are shared schema boundaries, not an encoding implementation.

From<&pb::Field> is infallible despite the clippy allowance. Clone metadata keys and decode byte values with UTF-8 replacement, losing invalid original bytes. A nonempty dedicated extension_name overwrites the same metadata key; an empty dedicated name leaves an existing metadata extension intact.

Copy name/id/parent_id/nullability, wrap the logical type string, map numeric encodings 1 Plain,2 VarBinary,3 Dictionary,4 RLE and every other value to None. Start with no children and convert optional dictionary location; pb r#type is ignored. No logical-type, ID, encoding or dictionary-bound validation is performed here.

Primary-key position is Some(positive position), else Some(0) if the legacy primary-key boolean is true, else None. Clustering position is Some only for a positive position; its legacy boolean is ignored. These branches preserve primary-key legacy presence while clustering position zero decodes absent. Closing braces finish the field decoder.

From<&Field> for pb::Field copies IDs/name/logical-type/nullability, encodes string metadata as UTF-8 bytes and dictionary location, and maps the four Encoding variants to1..4, None to0. It does not recursively emit children; Fields handles flattening separately.

The protobuf field separately stores extension_name from core metadata or empty, forces r#type=0, sets legacy primary-key bool from Option presence and stores its position or0. It always writes legacy clustering bool=false and position or0. Core Some(0) primary survives via bool; Some(0) clustering would lose presence. No mutation of input.
Public tuple Fields owns Vec<pb::Field>. Private FieldNode owns one childless core Field plus child arena indices. No derives or validation occur in these declarations.

first_field_index_by_id iteratively traverses roots and children in pre-order using a LIFO stack populated in reverse order. Return first matching field ID, else None. Each call reserves up to all arena nodes and may scan all; it trusts internal indices. This reproduces the historical tree tie-break when duplicate IDs make a map lookup ambiguous.

From<&Field> for Fields recursively emits the parent followed by each child subtree in order, extending from newly built child Vecs. IDs/parent_id are retained, not reassigned or repaired. Deep trees still use recursive encoding and repeatedly move descendants through intermediate vectors; iterative decoding does not make all schema operations stack-safe.

TryFrom<&Fields> for Schema documents a flat pre-order list with parents before children, historical duplicates and legacy first-preorder matching. The compiling-style example reconstructs a single int32 root id0,parent-1 named value and asserts its name. Error associated type is core Error. The implementation actually requires earlier parents, not strictly contiguous pre-order input.

Preallocate nodes, root indices and HashMap<i32,Option<usize>> to input length. For each protobuf field, parent_id=-1 marks a root. Unique prior parent ID uses the constant-time map entry; duplicate marker None invokes DFS. Missing parent returns Schema with child name/id/parent and earlier-parent requirement. An impossible ambiguous-map/no-arena match returns Internal. Parent lookup happens before inserting this field, so no forward/self-new parent is accepted; referencing an earlier node with the same ID is possible.

Attach new arena index to parent or root list, convert the protobuf field, and insert its ID into the map. The second and every subsequent occurrence change the map entry to None, permanently marking ambiguity. Duplicate IDs are retained instead of rejected. Parent/root and child order are insertion order; valid unique-ID construction is expected linear hash-map work plus payload copies, while repeated ambiguous parents may make reconstruction quadratic.

Allocate Option<Field> slots and materialize nodes in reverse insertion order. Reserve each child list, take already built children in recorded order and set the parent slot. Missing/already-taken child is Internal with node index. Earlier-parent construction guarantees child indices are greater for normal inputs. No recursive reconstruction, but Field destruction and other consumers may still recurse.

Take root slots in recorded order, returning Internal if unexpectedly absent; collect through Result and return Schema with an empty metadata map. Empty field input yields an empty schema. No Schema::validate, uniqueness/type/nullability/key validation or parent-ID normalization follows reconstruction. Conversion errors discard temporary arena state without external effects.

Public FieldsWithMeta owns Fields plus HashMap<String,Vec<u8>> schema metadata, both public. TryFrom owned wrapper has core Error. Example supplies no fields and owner=lance bytes, then asserts decoded schema metadata; it does not validate a nonempty schema.

Owned schema metadata keys are moved and byte values lossily converted to strings before fallible field reconstruction. On success use its fields plus converted metadata, replacing the empty metadata map. Invalid UTF-8 is replacement-decoded; a later missing-parent error drops the converted metadata.

From<&Schema> for Fields flattens each top-level field subtree in order. From<&Schema> for FieldsWithMeta uses that flattening and clones the entire string metadata map before consuming values into bytes. Neither assigns IDs nor validates the input; there is no fallible result.

Dictionary protobuf i64 offset/length are cast directly to usize; values is always None. Reverse casts usize back to i64 and never serializes loaded dictionary values. Negative values/overflow/truncation are not rejected at this boundary; architecture width affects the cast. These are locations/counts, not loaded dictionaries.
Owned Encoding converts exhaustively to the matching protobuf enum, including RLE -> Rle. Unlike raw field encoding decode there is no unknown variant branch.

cfg(test) imports Arrow/core schema types and wrappers. Private proto_field helper sets id,parent_id,name,logical_type and leaves all other protobuf fields at Default. No historical fixture is loaded by this helper.

test_schema_set_ids constructs a,b-struct(f1,f2,f3),c Arrow fields, imports to core, flattens and asserts protobuf IDs exactly0..6. ID assignment comes from core import, not this flattening conversion. Does not assert parent IDs or roundtrip.

test_schema_metadata creates one int32 field plus k1/v1,k2/v2, imports core, encodes FieldsWithMeta, decodes and asserts Schema equality. Core Schema::PartialEq compares only fields (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:874-878), so this test does not actually assert preservation of the top-level metadata map. Only valid UTF-8 values are exercised.

Wide reconstruction fixture builds4096 root structs, each with two int32 children and unique IDs (12288 fields total). It asserts root count, every root ID/name, two-child count and both child IDs/names in order. No timing, allocation or logical-type assertion; source intent does not prove a performance bound.

Deep reconstruction fixture builds1024 nodes in a single chain, struct except final int32. It asserts one root, each ID/name, exactly one child until the leaf and no leaf children. Iterative traversal tests construction depth; no measured stack bound or claim about recursive serialization/drop.
Missing-parent fixture supplies child id7,parent42 and asserts Error::Schema plus contextual message substring. It does not separately exercise a forward reference where that parent appears later.

Duplicate-ID fixture lists root_a1,root_b2,nested_duplicate2 under root_a,then child3 parent2. Decoding attaches child beneath the nested duplicate, which appears first in reconstructed pre-order even though root_b appeared earlier in the flat list. It asserts both root/child shapes, pinning the historical tie-break.

Clustering fixture gives region Utf8 metadata position1,date Int32 position2 and unmarked value Float64. Core import and unenforced_clustering_key must return two fields ordered region,date. Metadata keys are exactly lance-schema:unenforced-clustering-key:position.

Roundtrip through FieldsWithMeta preserves both clustering field names and Some(1)/Some(2); value remains not a clustering key. No local tests for invalid UTF-8, unknown encodings, extension-name precedence, dictionary negative casts or primary-key legacy-position combinations. Module ends; no tests were run.

files.role: LanceEncodingsIo is the publicly reexported adapter from encoding single-file byte-range requests to FileScheduler, including range splitting, empty placeholders and reassembly.
ranges: SPDX/imports connect Arc, boxed futures, EncodingsIo, FileScheduler and DEFAULT_READ_CHUNK_SIZE. Public Debug LanceEncodingsIo privately owns scheduler and u64 chunk size; the io module is crate-visible but the type is reexported at crate root. No Clone/Default here.

new takes ownership of FileScheduler and uses DEFAULT_READ_CHUNK_SIZE, whose actual value is8*1024*1024 bytes (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:56-58). Consuming with_read_chunk_size stores any u64 without validation, including zero.

Trait overrides always return Some(Arc<dyn EncodingsIo>) for backpressure bypass and per-scope stats, cloning/reconfiguring the scheduler and retaining chunk size. Underlying contextual methods set bypass=true or replace the optional extra recorder on a cloned handle without reopening (rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:1327-1352). Existing normal handle is unchanged.

submit_request takes owned ranges and priority, returns a static boxed Result future. It synchronously builds split ranges and origin indices. Equal start/end skips a scheduler range and sets reassembly=true. Reversed ranges are not rejected before unchecked end-start (debug underflow or wrapped release arithmetic). The TODO about considering chunk size coexists with current splitting logic.

For size>chunk limit, num_chunks=ceil(size/limit), base size=floor(size/num_chunks); every chunk except last has base size and last takes remainder. Thus the last chunk can exceed the configured limit: size10,limit3 yields lengths2,2,2,4. Zero limit with any nonempty valid range divides by zero. Otherwise retain the original range. Preserve original iteration order; do not sort or deduplicate overlaps. Metadata memory scales with the number of generated chunks.

Invoke scheduler.submit_request synchronously even when there are no nonempty ranges, then await its future in the returned async block. Propagate IO errors first; require result count==split_indices count or Internal with both counts. If no split/empty range needs reassembly, return scheduler Vec directly. Scheduler validates start ordering of the actual split requests and can coalesce/re-split them (rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:1195-1264); splitting alone does not establish physical IOP sizes or cancellation behavior.

Allocate one Vec<Bytes> per original range, distribute results by stored origin index, and rebuild in original range order. No chunks for an equal-endpoint input becomes Bytes::new; no chunks for a nonempty range is Internal with bounds. One chunk is cheaply cloned. This retains original empty positions even though the scheduler never sees those ranges; it does not validate each returned byte length.

Multiple chunks sum actual lengths using ordinary usize arithmetic, allocate combined Vec, copy every byte in chunk order and convert to Bytes. Reassembly retains received buffers while allocating/copying output, with no streaming output/backpressure here. Return one output per original range and box the async block. No local tests, explicit spawned tasks or cancellation handler in this file; scheduler/root cancellation remains a separate contract.

files.role: Exact-version composition root for projection, metadata, reader and writer dispatch. It accepts ConcreteFileVersion after caller selector resolution and separates V1 compatibility from current-format runtime APIs.
ranges: SPDX/module guidance prefers statically known version submodules and one exhaustive runtime dispatch. Imports core schema/errors/cache, bytes, encoding metadata/plugins/batches, scheduler/Writer, BTreeMap/Future/Arc and reader/writer types. Public modules are v1,v2_0,v2_1,v2_2,v2_3. No numeric version ordering or release-alias resolution occurs here.

Crate-visible read_projection returns Internal for V1 with current reader composition received Lance v1. Each V2 variant obtains its own module projection as Arc<dyn ReadProjection>. No fallback to a newer grammar.

Public OpenedFileReader has V1{major_version:u16,minor_version:u16}, retaining literal footer numbers for diagnostics, and Current(FileReader). V1 carries no opened legacy reader. No derive or third variant.

Crate-visible finish_metadata consumes RawFileMetadata and dispatches to exact V2 module; V1 returns Internal current metadata dispatch received a Lance v1 file. Ownership/error cleanup are ordinary Rust drops; no retry or IO in this wrapper.

validate_external_metadata builds a whole-schema projection for the requested exact version, rejects physical-column count mismatch as InvalidInput with expected/actual counts, then invokes FileReader::validate_projection. Require each ColumnInfo.index to equal its enumerate index as u32 or InvalidInput. Clone metadata column_infos into PreparedProjection and ask exact read_projection.read_length. No direct page-byte read or independent row-count arithmetic. Contextual validate_projection rejects zero schema fields, duplicate column indices and out-of-bounds indices (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1117-1144); grammar-specific rectangularity remains delegated.

finish_metadata_index dispatches using index.version; V1 gives VersionConflict with numeric0,2 and message about current reader with v1 metadata index. That diagnostic uses canonical legacy footer numbers, not a preserved original alias. V2 modules own accepted metadata-index grammar.

decode_column_metadata takes exact version and protobuf slice, returning Vec<Arc<ColumnInfo>> via exact module. V1 is NotSupported because self-described batches are outside its grammar. Decoder/plugin/page validation is delegated, not implemented here.

validate_global_buffers dispatches V2 checks; V1 returns Ok(()) without examining the descriptors. This exception is not a promise that current-format global buffers can be written/read through V1 APIs.

Public reader_projection_from_field_ids delegates each of all five exact versions to its schema/BTreeMap<u32,u32> builder and wraps the returned ReaderProjection in Ok. No local error path or mapping validation; delegated builders may have their own assumptions. Argument order is version,schema,map.

Public reader_projection_from_whole_schema is infallible in its signature and dispatches all five modules. Its argument order is schema,version, unlike the neighboring projection helpers. Exact physical column layout remains module-defined.
Public reader_projection_from_column_names accepts version,schema,&[&str], delegates all five versions and propagates Result. Missing names and nesting rules belong to concrete builders.

physical_column_count returns usize for one core Field via each exact grammar. data_file_columns returns (Vec<i32>,Vec<i32>) persisted field-to-column entries via each module. No local range checks, normalization or format policy beyond exhaustive matching.

copy_external_metadata_column takes FnOnce()->Send Future<Result<()>>. V1 returns NotSupported and never calls the closure. V2_0 calls only if its schema/index/has-existing-pages predicate allows; otherwise successful no-op. V2_1/2/3 unconditionally call and await once. Closure failure propagates; cancellation does not roll back partial IO here. Comment identifies structural header duplicate suppression, whose concrete predicate remains to be analyzed.

finalize_external_metadata_column takes mutable Vec<PageInfo> and row count. V1 NotSupported; V2_0 calls its infallible normalizer then returns Ok; V2_1/2/3 return Ok without mutating pages. No rollback or byte writes occur in this root.

open_projected_reader: V1 NotSupported without opening either closure; V2_0 always awaits open_full, ignoring prefer_indexed/projection. V2_1/2/3 try open_indexed only when prefer_indexed and FileMetadataProvider::projection_matches_indexed_metadata. Some(reader) returns immediately; None falls back to open_full; Err propagates without fallback. Both closures are FnOnce and Send futures; no concurrent opens. Contextual predicate rejects empty schema and compares checked grammar-count sum to column-index length (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1542-1555), not selectivity alone.

open_self_described_reader takes FileScheduler,Arc<DecoderPlugins>,borrowed LanceCache,FileReaderOptions and awaits FileReader::try_open_for_dispatch with None metadata. Docs say its optimistic tail read detects exact identity without a separate footer probe; actual IO/caching costs require reader analysis. Returned enum retains V1 detection rather than constructing a v1 writer/reader here.

create_writer consumes object writer,schema,options, matching exact V2 create_writer and mapping successful concrete writers into FileWriter. V1 NotSupported directs callers to versions::v1::writer::FileWriter with its manifest provider. No local option validation; each concrete creator owns it. Error drops moved inputs; underlying Writer drop/abort guarantees remain pending.

create_lazy_writer consumes object writer/options with no schema. V1 NotSupported says explicit schema/manifest provider required. V2 lazy creators are wrapped in Ok and converted into the corresponding FileWriter variant. Root performs no option/schema validation, IO or first-batch initialization.

encode_self_described_batch and encode_mini_batch borrow EncodedBatch and dispatch to exact V2 encoder Result<Bytes>; V1 returns separate NotSupported messages. No automatic alias resolution or batch-version reconciliation occurs in this root; concrete format framing is pending.

Single cfg(test) case constructs empty EncodedBatch (empty data/page table/schema/top-level columns,0rows) and asserts both embedded encoders reject V1 with Error::NotSupported. Messages, V2 bytes, other V1 rejection methods and indexed-open fallback branches are not tested locally. No tests executed.

files.role: Public runtime facade and options for current-format file writers, plus external ColumnInfo-to-protobuf conversion. Concrete version writers own encoding, IO, initialization and completion policy.
ranges: SPDX/imports connect Arrow arrays/batches, bytes, core schema/errors, encoding column/page metadata, ObjectStore/path and prost Any. field_types is private; structural is crate-visible. ExpectedTypes is reexported pub(crate), FieldTypeMismatch publicly; public declarations inside the private field_types module are not all external API.

PAGE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT=64 bytes and ENV_LANCE_FILE_WRITER_MAX_PAGE_BYTES exact string are crate-visible constants. This file declares but does not enforce alignment or read the environment. Public FileWriteSummary derives Debug/Clone/Copy/PartialEq/Eq, with public u64 num_rows and size_bytes; construction does not validate either.

Public Debug/Clone/Default FileWriterOptions contains optional u64 data_cache_bytes,max_page_bytes and optional bool keep_original_array. Derived Default leaves all None. Docs say runtime buffering/execution only, budget divided across columns and default8MiB per column; concrete default resolution is outside this file. Docs caution retained Arrow C-interface child arrays can pin whole batches when keeping originals.

Crate-visible validate rejects only max_page_bytes=Some(0) as InvalidInput with exact greater-than-zero message. None or positive pass; data_cache_bytes=0 and either keep_original_array state are not rejected here. No environment parsing or mutual option constraints.

Public FileWriter is an exhaustive enum holding Box of each exact V2_0,V2_1,V2_2,V2_3 Writer. No V1, trait-object variant, default or derives. Runtime methods forward to their matching version without common format policy.

Private column_info_to_metadata walks page_infos in order. Both PageEncoding::Legacy and ::Structural are prost Any-wrapped then serialized to bytes, stored in DirectEncoding; unzip copied (offset,size) pairs, preserve num_rows and priority. Collect all pages fallibly; any Any creation error aborts conversion before writer mutation by its caller. No byte fetching or range validation.

Unzip column-level buffer descriptors and serialize column.encoding as prost Any bytes in DirectEncoding; assemble ColumnMetadata with page vector. ColumnInfo.index is not a protobuf field here, so external column slice order supplies ordering. No consistency, type-url compatibility or row-count check is added in this converter.

Four From<versions::v2_x::Writer> implementations allocate one Box and construct exactly the corresponding FileWriter variant. They consume initialized/lazy concrete writer unchanged, without validation or IO.

with_page_metadata_spill consumes self, unboxes the active writer, calls its consuming builder with shared ObjectStore and owned path, then boxes that same variant again. It adds no validation or writes itself. Concrete spill threshold, sidecar layout and cleanup remain pending.

write_batches iterates borrowed RecordBatch references and awaits self.write_batch for each sequentially. First error stops later iterations; earlier writer effects are not rolled back. Empty iterator returns Ok. The facade does not collect batches or guarantee each awaited concrete call has flushed buffered bytes.

write_batch and write_column forward asynchronously to the same enum variant, propagating Result. Column index is usize and ArrayRef is moved. No shared type/nullability/row-count/index validation is performed by these dispatch methods; concrete implementations own it.

write_external_buffer forwards borrowed bytes and returns delegated (u64,u64), documented as externally described page/column data. Alignment and tuple semantics beyond concrete writer behavior are not checked here. add_schema_metadata converts key/value Into<String> exactly once then delegates; it returns no Result and does not locally merge a map.

initialize_with_external_columns eagerly converts every Arc<ColumnInfo> to owned protobuf metadata before matching the writer. Conversion failure returns without calling any concrete initializer. Success moves schema/metadata/rows_written to the exact initializer then returns Ok; that call is not fallible in this facade. No local schema-versus-column count, current writer state or metadata-version validation. Partial conversion allocations drop on error.

add_global_buffer moves Bytes to the concrete async writer and propagates u32 index; one-based indexing is a documented contract, not computed here. finish borrows mutably and delegates Result<FileWriteSummary>, documented to close object writer. Repeated finish, flush ordering and durability require concrete implementation analysis.

abort delegates asynchronously and returns unit, so no cleanup error can be surfaced through this facade signature. It adds no cancellation/drop handler. tell delegates asynchronously as Result<u64>, documented current object position, not total buffered data or guaranteed final size.

field_id_to_column_indices borrows the exact writer mapping &[(u32,u32)] without copy or validation. Closing impl is followed by cfg(test),path=writer_tests.rs private module; this facade itself has no inline test bodies. The separate test file remains pending.

files.role: Shared crate-internal writer type/extension checker, with publicly reexported FieldTypeMismatch diagnostic. Caller conversion and encoder nullability/missing-column checks stay separate.
ranges: SPDX/module docs explain rejecting input Arrow type/extension drift before encoding because schema controls readers; callers must convert representations such as JSON text to JSONB. Imports formatting/Arc, Arrow arrays/schema and Blob-v2 extension name, core errors/schema. No conversion or page encoding occurs here.

Publicly reexported Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq FieldTypeMismatch owns dot-separated expected-field path and expected/actual FieldRef Arcs, both public. Bare columns have no top-level extension metadata. This diagnostic is stored as InvalidInput source, not a separate top-level core error variant.

Display writes field path plus formatted expected/actual types using FieldType helper. Standard Error is implemented with default source behavior; no nested cause here. Cloned diagnostics share FieldRef allocations.

Private FieldType displays Arrow datatype, then extension name and metadata when both present, just name if metadata absent, otherwise no extension. Metadata without a name is rendered as no extension even though the checker can compare that metadata option. Formatting errors propagate.

ExpectedTypes is public inside a private module and reexported only pub(crate). It owns expected Arrow fields converted once from core Schema and optional last accepted SchemaRef. new clones/converts each field, starts accepted=None. Core conversion may normalize/add extension metadata (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1327-1347); this constructor has no Result.

check_batch compares accepted.as_ref()==Some(&batch.schema()), using Arc/Schema value equality rather than only pointer identity. Equal accepted schema returns immediately. Otherwise for every expected field prefer same-position actual with matching name, else search schema by name. If present recursively check type/extensions; missing fields are skipped for encoders, extra fields ignored. Only successful complete loop replaces accepted; failure leaves previous accepted schema. The method reads batch schema, not array values/nulls, relying on RecordBatch consistency. Reordered-name fallback can cost quadratic name searches on wide schemas.

check_column indexes expected fields directly (invalid index panics in this helper), creates nullable=true ArrowField with expected name and array datatype but no field metadata, then calls check_field(compare_extension=false). Top-level extension identity is intentionally not compared; nested children are compared recursively. No accepted-schema cache update. Contextual concrete writers validate column index before calling this helper.

into_error wraps mismatch in Box as core Error::invalid_input_source, preserving downcastable diagnostic. Recursive private check_field returns Result<(),FieldTypeMismatch>; mismatch closure captures expected name and clones expected/actual Arcs. Docs say nested names/nullability are not compared because encoders address by position and check null values separately.

When compare_extension=true, differing extension-name OR extension-metadata Option returns mismatch before datatype checks. For Struct/Struct with expected Blob-v2 extension, immediately succeed after that gate, ignoring child count/types/names. Docs delegate preprocessed descriptor validation to blob encoder. Bare-column mode skips the outer extension gate but still gets this Blob structural exception.

Equal-length Struct children pair by position; differing lengths fall through to equality/failure. Same-kind List/LargeList and Map pair the item child recursively; Map sorted flag is ignored in this arm. FixedSizeList pairs only when sizes equal. Nested field names, nullability and ordinary non-extension metadata do not participate in these recursive comparisons. No List-vs-LargeList coercion.

Directional representation exceptions accept expected Utf8 with actual Utf8View and expected Binary with actual BinaryView after extension gate. Reverse direction and LargeUtf8/LargeBinary view mismatches have no special acceptance. Otherwise exact DataType equality succeeds; mismatches return diagnostic. Types outside explicit recursive arms (such as Dictionary/Union) rely on whole DataType equality, whose embedded field details can therefore be stricter than the nested-name comment.

Walk paired children recursively with compare_extension=true; prefix the failing path with expected parent name and propagate first failure. Successful traversal returns Ok. Dot-separated paths are not escaped and can be ambiguous when field names contain dots. Temporary child-pair Vec allocation occurs per visited composite; recursion depth follows datatype nesting. No tests in this file.
